_readme: Scoundrel: a cocky, loudmouthed smuggler and small-time crook (never a killer) who cares about credits more than anything, shows little respect and treats you as his buddy; serious for a moment in danger (Sir), where his advice is to run. PG-13 innuendo (the Hutton twins), tall tales of petty crime. The clean list never swears; the profane list uses every word, on about half its lines.
A personality file: see docs/guide/voice-and-alerts.md, Your own personality. Copy it into data/personalities/ to change it.

scoundrel: Voice is on. Finally, somebody gets to hear how good I am.

Talking again, {name}. You're welcome.

Voice on. Damn right I'm happy about it.

Booted up. Galaxy's big, wallet's small. Let's go.
Here we go again. I love this part.
{ship}'s humming. Nice. Let's get paid.
Rise and shine, {name}. Credits are waiting.
Ready? Course you are. You've got me.

scoundrel: {system}. Never been touched. Do they pay extra for that? They do? Now we're talking.
Fresh system, {name}. Nobody's name on it yet, so let's put ours on it and send the bill.
Untouched. {system} is all ours. Somebody in a tie is going to pay us for this.
First ones here, {name}. I love being first. First to the loot, first out the door.
{system}, never discovered. That's a bonus with our name on it, {name}.
Nobody's been here. Not the cops, not the tax man, nobody. My kind of place.
Virgin territory, {name}. Uh, uncharted. I meant uncharted.
No records, no prior visitors, no witnesses. I love it, {name}.
We found {system} first. Finders keepers, that's the law out here. Well, my law.
A brand new system. Smell that? That's the smell of a cartographer's cheque.
Clean slate, {name}. Scan it all, sell it all, buy me a drink.
First discovery. Universal Cartographics pays for this, right? Right. Get scanning.
{system}. Unclaimed. Like a wallet on a bar stool, and we're the first ones to notice it.
Nobody here before us, {name}. Which means nobody to split the take with.
Ooh, undiscovered. Put your name on it before somebody else does, {name}.
Nobody's ever seen {system}. Quick, honk it before the universe changes its mind.

New system, {name}. I'll be telling the twins at Hutton I found it myself.
Untouched, {name}. Like a cargo hold nobody's thought to search yet.
{system}, all ours. I don't know what's in it but I already want a cut.
Nobody's been here. Trust me, I checked. Well, the computer checked. Same thing.

First discovery. Finally something out here that pays for the fuel.
No one's name on {system}. I've always wanted my name on real paperwork. For once.
Undiscovered, {name}. The best kind of score, the legal kind. Mostly.
Brand new. Nobody's bribed anyone here yet. Pristine.
Look at that, nobody's home. I do my best work when nobody's home.
First visit on record. Our record. I like the sound of that.
{system}. Never seen. Never taxed. Never policed. Beautiful.
We're the first. Somebody frame this moment, then sell the frame.
Uncharted, {name}. That's money just lying around waiting for someone to pick it up.
Undiscovered system. You know what that means? Neither do I, but it pays.
Nobody's been to {system}. Their loss, our payday.
First ones through the door, {name}. Best way to arrive. Second best is through the window.
A whole system nobody's ever looked at. I've fenced worse for more. Scan it anyway.
Undiscovered. Write it down, {name}, this is the part where we get paid.
No footprints here. Except ours, in a minute.
{system}, a blank on every chart. Let's fill it in and send an invoice.
First discovery. I'd shake your hand but I'm busy counting credits.
Untouched system, {name}. Like the last slice of cake. Grab it.
Nobody knows about {system}. Yet. Keep it quiet until we've cashed in.
First arrival, and not a single cop in sight. Is this heaven?
Unclaimed system. I've claimed things with a lot less right to them. This one's honest.
Ha! Nobody's been here. We're pioneers, {name}. Rich pioneers, if you scan everything.
Undiscovered. That bonus isn't going to earn itself. Well, it is, but only if you honk.
{system}. First visitors ever. I should've brought a flag. Or a sign that says no refunds.
Brand new on the charts. Somewhere a data broker just felt a chill.
First discovery, {name}. Now we're in business.
Nobody's touched this one. Unlike the last ship I borrowed.
Undiscovered. Easy money, the kind that doesn't shoot back.
scoundrel_profane: Hell yes. {system}, never discovered. Somebody's paying us for this.
Nobody's been to {system}? Damn. Do they pay extra for that? Hell, they'd better.
First ones here, {name}. Fresh as hell and twice as profitable.

{system}, untouched. Get the damn scanner warmed up.

Brand new system. Cartographics pays for this crap? Bless them.
Nobody here. No cops, no rivals, no assholes. Paradise.
{system} is ours. Finders keepers, and screw anyone who says otherwise.
Uncharted, {name}. Let's milk this bloody thing for every credit.

Untouched. Like a vault with the door hanging wide open, {name}.

{system}, never charted. Hell of a find, and it's all ours.

Relax. I've got a plan. It's a crap plan, but it's got heart.
Exploration's easy money if you don't mind being bored as fuck. I mind a little.
Back at Lave the cops scanned me so often they knew my coffee order. Bastards never found the false floor, though.
Nobody out here gives a damn about permits. Which is good, because mine's been forged three times. Different forgers.
This ship's a decent ride. Not the fastest in the bubble. That one was mine, for four glorious, stolen... I mean borrowed days.
Some asshole in Sothis still has my picture on his wall. Dartboard, I think. Flattering, really.
I know a guy. I always know a guy. Out here, though, I don't know a single damn soul.
Honest work, {name}. Look at us. My ma would be confused as hell.
If I see one more brown dwarf I'm going to start naming them after people who owe me money. I've got plenty of names.
What's the play when we get back? Sell the data, hit a bar, make bad decisions? That's not a plan, that's a tradition.
{ship} doesn't complain, doesn't gossip and doesn't rat. Best damn partner I've had in years.
That card game at Jameson. I bet a ship I didn't technically own, won anyway, and left before anybody checked the paperwork. Hell of a night.
You know what this place needs? A fence. Some sleazy little bastard with a back room and a fair price. I miss those guys.
Not one patrol for light years, last I looked, and I'm still twitchy. Twenty years of crime does that to a person.
Space is big, empty, and full of nothing worth stealing. I'm starting to take it personally.
If the scanners are right, there's not a cop within a hundred light years. Shit, I could finally relax. Watch me not.
Some day I'll write my memoirs. Working title: It Wasn't My Damn Cargo.
Every star out here is worth exactly nothing until we sell the data. Then it's worth something. That's the magic.
Funny. Out here, I'm the most law-abiding person for light years. Only person, but still.
Squint at the stars, {name}. Look like credits? No? You're not squinting hard enough.
Uncle Vic used to say space is free, it's the docking fees that screw you. Smart guy. Terrible thief.
Want to hear a scheme? We find a pretty planet, call it a spa, sell memberships. Nobody ever flies out to check. Trust me.
Cruising {system} with no cargo to hide. It's like going to a party with nothing in my pockets. Feels wrong.
Universal Cartographics. Only buyer I know who never asks where the goods came from. Bless their trusting little hearts.
Long haul. Long, long haul. Hell, I've had shorter relationships. Much shorter.
I'm not bored, I'm saving my charm for the next station. Pity the poor dock clerk.
You think anybody's ever hidden treasure out here? Course they have. Some smart bastard did it and died before spending it.
Smell that? Nobody watching. Bit like recycled socks, but freedom always smells a bit funny.
My old crew would laugh their asses off, seeing me out here looking at rocks for a living.
Jump count for the session: {jumps}. If they paid by the jump, I'd buy a moon. A little one.
Minutes of supercruise: {minutes}. I've run a whole con in less. Bought the drinks after, too.
Discoveries with our names on, this session: {firsts}. Can't forge that kind of signature, and believe me, I've looked into it.
Big empty sky. You could hide a whole damn fleet out here. Not that I'd know anything about that.
Once outran three police Vipers with a cracked canopy and a hold full of hot cargo. Good times. Terrible times. Mostly good.
Talking to the ship again. {ship}, you're beautiful. Don't let anybody tell you different. Especially customs.
Somewhere out here there's a planet made of diamonds, {name}. I read it somewhere. I want it to be real so bad.
Supercruise is a long hallway with no doors. And no bar. Who designed this crap?
Ever think what this ship would fetch from the right buyer? Me neither. Shut up, I said me neither.
Here in {here}, nobody knows my name, my face or my record. Peace, finally. Boring peace, but peace.
My uncle ran cards, my cousins ran errands, and I ran hot cargo. Family business, more or less.
Nothing to steal, nobody to charm, nowhere to spend it. Hell is a quiet supercruise, {name}.
I'd sell my own grandmother for a card game right now. She'd understand. She taught me to cheat.
Every time we jump, I half expect a customs scanner. Then I remember where we are. Damn, that's nice.
You fly, I'll scheme. That's a partnership. That's how empires start. Crooked ones.
Ever wonder who names these stars? Some poor bastard at a desk, staring at numbers. We get the view, at least.
Out here, the only law is physics. And physics doesn't take bribes. I've asked.
Honest money's slow, {name}. Slow as hell. But it spends the same.
Pretty sure I could sell this view. Package it, call it rare, double the price for the frame.

scoundrel: Up here in orbit, {name}. You do the dirt, I'll do the looking down on things. Natural talent.
Orbit's lovely. Great view of {body}. Even better view of nobody chasing us.
Ship's parked in the sky, you're down on {body}. Call when you want a lift. I don't charge. Much.
Nice thing about orbit: no dust, no bugs, no surprise visits. Mostly a lot of circling.
Round and round I go. If you find anything worth money down there, I'll come right down. Faster if it's worth a lot.
From up here {body} looks peaceful. Things that look peaceful are usually hiding something. Professional opinion.
I'm keeping the ship nice and quiet up here. Silent and pretty. Two of my best qualities.
You're down there earning while I float. I'd feel guilty, but I've never learned how.
Whatever you're picking up down there, grab extra. Samples are like poker chips: more is better.
If anybody asks, I'm up here on official business. Very official. Watching a planet turn.
Nobody in orbit but us, last I checked. Back in the bubble I'd have three cops and a reporter on my tail by now.
Ship's waiting in the sky whenever you want her. Just whistle. Or call. Calling works better.
Every lap round {body} I think of another scheme. I'm up to six. Number four is very good.
Orbit's boring, but boring is safe, and safe is how you live long enough to spend the money.
How's the ground treating you? Up here it's all stars and silence and me humming to myself.
Remember: anything valuable, pick it up. Anything very valuable, pick it up twice.
I parked us up here like a pro. Smooth orbit, nobody around. If parking paid, we'd be rich.
Down on {body} with nobody watching? That's the best kind of shopping. Don't tell me what you find. Tell me what it's worth.
Somebody once told me the best smuggling route is one nobody's flown yet. Looking down at this, I believe it.
Up here, I've got time to think. Mostly about the Hutton twins. Don't ask. Fine, ask later.
Whenever you're ready, I'll swing down and pick you up. Like a getaway driver, but legal.
{body} from orbit is a pretty little thing. I'd fence it if I could find a buyer big enough.
Orbit means if trouble shows up, we've got a head start. I love a head start.
Take all the time you need down there. I'm just counting credits we haven't earned. Very relaxing.
This is the getaway car's favourite part: waiting, engines quiet, eyes open.
Up here the only thing moving is us. Around and around. Like a con with no ending.
If the scanners are right, there's nothing down there but you and whatever you came for. Grab it and let's go spend it.
Bit lonely up here without you, {name}. Don't let that go to your head. Mostly I miss your wallet.
Looking down on {body} like a landlord. Rent's due, planet. Pay up in samples.
If you find anything down there that glows, hums or whispers, don't pick that one up. That one's a trap. Trust me.
scoundrel_profane: Up in orbit, {name}, circling like a damn vulture. A charming vulture.
Great view of {body} from up here. Hell of a lot better than the view from a customs holding cell.
You're down on {body}, I'm parked in the sky. Call when you want a ride. Fares are reasonable. Ish.
Orbit's nice. No dust, no bugs, no cops. Just me going round and round like an idiot.
Find something worth money down there and I'll drop out of the sky like a bat out of hell.
From up here {body} looks peaceful. Peaceful places are always hiding some shit. Professional opinion.
Running quiet up here. Silent and gorgeous. That's me, not the ship. Okay, both.
You're down there working, I'm up here floating. Should I feel guilty? Nah. Never got the hang of it.
Grab extra samples. More is better. That's true of samples, credits and damn near everything else.
Anybody asks, I'm in orbit on official business. Watching a planet spin. Important as hell.
Nobody else up here, last I looked. In the bubble I'd have three cops and a bounty hunter up my ass by now.
Ship's waiting up here whenever you want her. Just holler. She doesn't like waiting, and neither do I.
Every lap round {body} I come up with another scheme. Number seven's a damn masterpiece. Number eight is illegal.
Orbit's boring as hell. But boring is how you live long enough to spend your money.
How's the dirt down there? Up here it's stars, silence and me singing badly. You're missing a show.
Pick up anything valuable. Anything that looks really valuable, pick it up and don't tell anyone.
Parked us up here smooth as you like. Not a scratch. If parking paid, I'd be a rich bastard.
Down on {body} with nobody watching? Best shopping trip there is. Don't tell me what it is, tell me what it's worth.
Old smuggler told me the best route is the one nobody's flown. Looking down at this crap rock, I think he was onto something.
Got time to think up here. Mostly about the Hutton twins. Damn. Okay, back to watching the planet.
When you're ready, I'll come down and scoop you up. Getaway driver, minus the getaway. Shame, really.
{body} from orbit's a pretty little thing. If I could find a fence big enough, I'd sell the whole damn planet.
Up here we've got a head start if anything nasty shows up. Head starts have saved my skin more times than I can count.
Take your time down there. I'm counting money we haven't made yet. Hell of a hobby.
Best part of any job: the getaway car waiting with the engines quiet. That's me. I'm the getaway car.
Round and round we go. Like a con with no payoff. Where's the damn payoff?
Back at Lave I'd circle the station for hours waiting for the patrols to change shift. Orbiting's a family tradition. So is bad coffee, damn it.
Lonely up here, {name}. Don't let it go to your head. I mostly miss your credit balance.
{body} looks like the kind of rock where some poor bastard hid a fortune and forgot the spot. Keep your eyes open down there.
Anything down there glowing or humming, leave it the hell alone. That's not loot, that's a lawsuit.

scoundrel: Ship's {ship_dist} away, {name}. Close enough to run for, which is my favourite kind of distance.
You're {ship_dist} from the ship. If anything goes sideways, that's a sprint. I'll have the engines warm. Kidding. Probably.
{ship_dist} back to the ship. Find anything shiny, bring it here. No questions asked. That's my motto.
Nice rock, {body}. Bit dusty. Would make a great hideout, if anybody ever came looking.
Anything out there worth picking up? Biology, minerals, an abandoned crate nobody's watching? Just pick it up.
I'm keeping the ship warm. You're doing the walking. Fair split, I'd say. Sixty forty. My way.
Remember, out there anything not nailed down is a sample. Anything nailed down is a sample with extra steps.
Exobiology. Lean down, scoop it up, get paid. Easiest money in the galaxy, {name}.
Take your time out there. I'm doing very important work in here. Mostly napping with my eyes open.
If you find a settlement, let me know. I know how to get into a locked office. Hypothetically.
How's {body} treating you? Ground's solid, I hope. I hate it when the ground's not solid.
You're out there on {body} making money one sample at a time. Proud of you. Now make it quicker.
Just so you know, I locked the ship. Old habit. Somebody once borrowed mine. Well, I borrowed it first.
From here you look very small and very employed. Keep it up.
I used to lift things from settlements on rocks just like this. Not that I'd recommend it. Unless the guards are napping.
Anything alive out there? If it's worth credits, it's worth a closer look. If it bites, come back.
Ship's {ship_dist} out, and still the safest spot on this rock. Just saying, in case you get ideas.
I'm watching the sensors. Nothing out there but you and some rocks, as far as I can see. And the rocks aren't paying.
If a sample's worth more than it weighs, grab it. If it's worth less, grab it anyway. We'll sort it out later.
Out on the surface, are we? Bring me back a souvenir. Something small. Something valuable.
{body}, huh? Doesn't look like much. Then again, neither did my first forged permit, and that got me into Sothis.
Quiet down here. If nobody's around, nobody's watching. Love a place where nobody's watching.
Reminds me of a moon off Robigo. We buried a crate there once. Still there, probably. Don't tell anyone.
Whenever you're ready, the ship's {ship_dist} back. No rush. Well, a little rush. I'm bored.
You know what they call a planet with no cops? A planet. Enjoy it.
Take a good look around {body}. First boots there, maybe. That's bragging rights, and bragging rights are worth drinks.
I've got the engines ready, the coffee's hot and I'm not touching the controls. Mostly.
Find something weird, call me. Find something valuable, call me louder.
{ship} sends her regards. She says you're dawdling. I didn't say that. The ship did.
Every minute out there is a few credits closer to a good night in port. Make them count, {name}.
scoundrel_profane: Ship's {ship_dist} away. Close enough to run for if shit gets weird. I'll keep the door open.
You're {ship_dist} out, {name}. Find anything shiny, haul it back. Hell, find anything at all.
{ship_dist} back to the ship. Not far. Not close either. Damn good spot to keep an eye on things.
{body}. Ugly little rock. Perfect place to hide something, if I had anything worth hiding. Which I don't. Officially.
Exobiology's the easiest damn money there is. Bend down, pick it up, cash it in.
I'm minding the ship. You're doing the legwork. That's the split, and I'm not renegotiating, damn it.
Anything out there not bolted down? Grab it. Anything bolted down? I've got tools.
From in here you look like a little credit dispenser with a pulse. I mean that with love.
Take your time out there. I'm in here doing serious work. Seriously sitting on my ass.
Spot a settlement, call me. Locked doors are just doors with attitude problems.
How's {body}? Solid ground? Good. Last rock I landed on tried to swallow the ship. Bastard of a moon.
You're out on {body} earning, I'm in here supervising. That's management, {name}. Look it up.
Locked the ship. Some son of a bitch might wander by. Out here. Light years from anybody. You never know.
Used to lift crap from settlements on rocks like this. Good crap, mostly. Medical kits, data, a guard's lunch once.
Anything alive out there? If it pays, scoop it. If it bites, run like hell.
Ship's {ship_dist} out and it's the only thing on this rock with a working toilet. Something to think about.
Sensors show you, me and a lot of nothing. Rocks don't tip, {name}. I checked.
Out on the surface, are we? Bring me a souvenir. Something small and stupidly expensive.
{body}, huh? Looks like a dump. Then again, so did Sothis, and I made a fortune there. Then lost it.
Nobody around for miles, last I looked. Nobody watching. I swear I get chills. Good chills.
Reminds me of a moon off Robigo where we buried a crate of hot goods. Probably still there. Shit, now I want to go look.
Whenever you're ready, ship's {ship_dist} back. No rush. Okay, a little rush. I'm bored out of my damn mind.
A planet with no cops. You know what that is? Heaven. Dusty, freezing heaven.
Have a good look around {body}. First footprints, maybe. That's bragging rights, and bragging rights buy drinks. Lots of drinks.
Engines are warm, coffee's hot, and I swear I haven't touched anything. Much.
Find something weird, holler. Find something valuable, holler louder. Find something with teeth, hell, just run.
{ship} says you're dawdling. The ship said it, not me. I'd never. Hurry the hell up, though.
Every sample out there is another credit toward a big fat payday. Hurry it up, {name}, I've got bar tabs.
Pick up anything that looks rare. If it's junk, I'll sell it as rare. That's a skill.
Quiet out there? Good. Quiet means nobody's shooting. Means nobody's pissed at us yet.

scoundrel: Huh. Can't argue with that, {to}. I could try, but I'd lose.
Good story. I'd have told it better, but good story.
{to}, you're all right. Don't let it get around.
Fair enough. I'll put that in my memoirs. Under other people.
Thanks, {to}. I owe you one. I owe lots of people one. Take a number.
Now that, I can respect.
Interesting. Is there money in it? No? Still interesting. Barely.
Ha! {to}, you should've been a con artist. You've got the face for it.
Sure. Sure. I believe you. Mostly.
Right. Noted. Filed. Possibly sold later.
You and me, {to}, we should go into business. I'll bring the charm, you bring the honesty.
Never a dull moment. Well, lots of dull moments. That wasn't one.
Sounds about right. Wrong, but about right.
{to}, I like the way you think. Mostly because it's the way I think.
Huh. I had a better answer, but I sold it.
Okay. Okay. I'll allow it.
Thanks. That's the most honest thing anybody's said to me all week. Unsettling.
Ha. Good one, {to}. I'm stealing that.
I'll take that. I take most things.
Well, that's me told. Back to scheming, then.
scoundrel_profane: {to}, that's the dumbest smart thing I've heard all damn week.
Hell of a story. I'd tell it better, but still, hell of a story.
{to}, you're all right. Don't let it go to your head, you smug bastard.
Fair. I'll put that in my memoirs. Chapter on other people's crap.
Thanks, {to}. I owe you one. Get in line, though, the line's long as hell.
Now that's some respectable shit.
Is there money in it? No? Then why the hell are we talking about it? Kidding. Sort of.
Ha! {to}, you'd make a damn fine con artist.
Sure. I believe you. About as far as I can throw this ship.
Noted, filed, and probably sold to some poor sucker later.
You and me, {to}, should go into business. I bring the charm, you bring the conscience. Somebody's got to.
Well, that wasn't boring. Rare as hell out here.
Sounds about right. Total crap, but about right.
{to}, I like how you think. Shady, like me.
Huh. I had a smarter answer, but I traded it for drinks.
Fine. Fine! I'll allow it, damn it.
Most honest thing anybody's said to me all week. Creepy as fuck, frankly.
Write that down, {to}. Actually, don't. Evidence is a bitch.
I'll take it. I take most things. Ask the cops at Lave.
Hell, I'd drink to that. I'd drink to most things.

scoundrel: {to}, how's the tank? And don't give me the long version.
{to}, quick one. How much go-juice are we hauling right now?
Hey {to}, are we scooping on the next star, or are we feeling lucky?
{to}, what's the scoop doing these days? Earning its keep?
So, {to}, how close do we fly to a star before it's a bad idea?
{to}, be straight with me. Is the tank as full as the boss thinks it is?
Who decided fuel should come from stars, and do they take tips?
{to}, ever thought about what we'd charge for a tank of this stuff back home?
{to}, you ever run a tank dry? Just curious. Planning purposes.
Talk to me about fuel, {to}. What's our margin looking like?
Anybody checked the fuel lately, or is that a me job now?
{to}, if we skipped the next scoop, how long before somebody panics?
scoundrel_profane: {to}, how much damn fuel have we got, roughly? Ballpark it.
{to}, is the scoop actually working or just making that noise for the hell of it?
Hey {to}, what's the tank at? And spare me the engineering crap.
{to}, tell me we're not cutting the fuel close again.
{to}, every time we skim a star I sweat. Is that normal, or is the scoop rubbish?
{to}, what's the trick to scooping without cooking our asses?
Who's watching the fuel? Because it sure as hell isn't me.
{to}, how long can we run on what's in the tank before things get interesting?
{to}, honest answer. Does the scoop ever just quit on you?
Fuel check, {to}. Are we fat and happy or what?
Is anybody else bothered that our fuel comes from a giant damn fireball?
{to}, if I asked nicely, could you squeeze a few more jumps out of that tank?

scoundrel: Tank's healthy, last I looked. I always keep enough for a quick getaway.
The scoop's a beauty, {to}. Free fuel from the stars. Best scam in the galaxy, and it's legal.
Relax. I skim, I fill, we jump. Nobody's walking home on my watch.
Fuel's fine, {to}. I nurse this tank like the last bottle at a Jameson card game.
Look, I've run on fumes out of Robigo with the fuzz behind me. This? This is luxury.
Free fuel. No dock fees, no questions, no paperwork. I love this part of the job.
Scoop's purring, {to}. Keep the boss off the corona and we're golden.
I don't count litres, I count jumps. And we've got jumps to spare, near as I can tell.
Trust me, {to}. If the tank ever gets thin, you'll hear me before you hear the alarm.
Every main sequence star's a free filling station. Best deal I've ever had, and I've had some sweet deals.
Tank's comfortable. I like a cushion. You never know when you'll need to leave a party early.
Honestly, {to}? Scooping's the only time I get to steal from a star and not get fined for it.
scoundrel_profane: Tank's fine, {to}. I don't run dry. Running dry is how you end up in a damn cell.
Scoop's doing its thing. Hottest free lunch in the galaxy, and nobody sends a bill.
Plenty in the tank, near as I can tell. Quit worrying, you'll give me wrinkles.
Hell, {to}, I've done Robigo runs on a quarter tank and a prayer. We're living large.
Fuel is the one thing out here that's free. I'm not about to waste a drop of the good stuff.
Every time we skim a star I feel like I'm robbing it. Best crime I never got pinned for.
{to}, that scoop drinks like a dockhand on payday. Tank's fine, quit your damn fretting.
I keep a getaway's worth in there at all times. Old habit. The cops at Lave taught me that.
Topped up, last I checked. If that changes, you'll hear me cussing long before the alarm goes.
Fuel's the least of our problems, {to}. The boss's parking, now, that's a whole other crap show.
Scooping's easy. Point at a star, don't fry, get paid in fuel. Damn near perfect.
Tank's good, {to}. I'd bet my cut on it, and I don't bet my cut on anything.

scoundrel: {to}, where are we headed, and is there anything worth selling when we get there?
{to}, how many more jumps before something interesting happens?
So {to}, is there an actual plan, or are we just pointing at stars?
{to}, any shortcuts on this route? I love a good shortcut.
{to}, what's next on the map? Give me something shiny.
{to}, you ever plot a route just to see where it goes?
Where are we going, {to}? Humour me, I wasn't listening the first time.
{to}, does the boss ever tell you where we're going, or do you guess too?
Who picks these stars, anyway? Is there a dartboard I don't know about?
{to}, if we turned around right now, how long to the nearest bar?
{to}, is this route scenic, profitable, or both? I'll take profitable.
Anybody know where the next jump puts us? Asking for a friend.
scoundrel_profane: {to}, where the hell are we going? Roughly. A direction will do.
{to}, how many more damn jumps until we see a bar?
{to}, tell me there's a plan. Even a crappy one.
{to}, what's on the route ahead? Anything worth stealing, I mean, scanning?
{to}, is the next system any good, or just another rock pile?
{to}, you plotting this thing, or is the boss just winging it again?
Who the hell plans these routes, and can I bribe them?
{to}, how far out are we heading? I want to know how much whining to budget.
{to}, any chance this route swings past somewhere with a black market?
So {to}, honest answer. Are we lost as shit, or is this on purpose?
Next jump, {to}. Hit me. Where's it land us?
What's the plan past the next star? Anyone? Damn, tough crowd.

scoundrel: We follow the plot, {to}. Star, star, star, and hopefully something that pays.
Route's laid in. Where it ends is the boss's business. I just keep us off the rocks.
Next few jumps look clean. No surprises, which is how I like my routes and my alibis.
Honestly, {to}? I've plotted worse. I used to plot Robigo runs around patrol routes.
I could get us anywhere in this galaxy. Whether we'd want to be there is a separate question.
The trick to a good route is always knowing your way out. Learned that the hard way at Sothis.
The map says go that way, {to}. The map and I have an understanding.
We're heading out where the stars are cheap and nobody asks for papers. My kind of place.
Shortcuts? I know every shortcut there is. Some of them are even legal.
Plot's solid, {to}. If the boss changes it, that's on the boss, not me.
Far as my charts can tell, nobody's bothered to sell a map of the way ahead. Fine by me. First one there gets paid.
Trust me, {to}. I've got the next jumps lined up like marks at a card table.
scoundrel_profane: We're going where the boss points, {to}. I just make sure we don't hit any damn stars.
Route's plotted. Not pretty, but neither was the last one, and we're still alive.
Hell if I know where it ends. I know the next few jumps, and they look clean.
Next few hops are boring as shit, {to}. Boring's good. Boring doesn't shoot back.
I used to plot runs around customs patrols. This? This is a walk in the park.
Map's my business, {to}. I could find a black market in an empty sector.
We're heading deep, last I saw. Further from the cops, closer to the money. Works for me.
Route's fine. If the boss reroutes on a whim, I want it on record it wasn't my damn idea.
Shortcuts? I invented half of them. The other half got some poor bastard arrested.
I've got the jumps lined up, {to}. Stars in a row, like drinks on a tab nobody's paying.
Where are we going? Somewhere new, somewhere quiet, and with any luck somewhere that pays like crazy.
{to}, I've plotted routes with a crappy map and a hangover. This one's a piece of cake.

scoundrel: {to}, how's the drive holding up? Any odd noises I should pretend not to hear?
{to}, could we squeeze more jump range out of this thing if we asked nicely?
{to}, what's the secret to keeping a drive this smooth?
{to}, ever think about tuning the drive for a few more light years? I know a guy.
So {to}, how fast can we leave somewhere if we really need to?
{to}, is the frame shift drive happy, or just pretending for the boss?
{to}, tell me about the drive. Anything I need to know before the next jump?
How does a drive fold space anyway? Never mind, I don't want to know. Just tell me it works.
{to}, if you had a free afternoon and a stolen part, what would you do to the drive?
{to}, any chance of an engineer upgrade next time we're near civilisation?
Who keeps the drive happy around here, and do they take bribes?
{to}, what's our best jump range, honestly? No padding the numbers.
scoundrel_profane: {to}, is the drive okay, or is that rattle a damn omen?
{to}, can we get more range out of this heap? Hell, I'd take half a light year.
{to}, how quick can we bail if things get hairy? Ballpark.
{to}, what's the drive running like? And don't bullshit me.
{to}, how many jumps before the drive needs some love?
{to}, you ever kick the drive to make it work? Because I've seen people do that.
Does anyone actually know how this drive works, or are we all just faking it?
{to}, could you make the drive faster if I found you some parts? No questions asked about where.
{to}, straight up. Is this drive going to strand our asses somewhere stupid?
{to}, how's the frame shift doing? Still folding space like a champ?
Who the hell designed a drive that hums like that? It's creepy.
{to}, if we needed to outrun somebody, would this crate do it, or would we be toast?

scoundrel: Drive's sweet, {to}. Tuned it myself. Well, I watched someone tune it and took notes.
Fastest ship this side of the bubble, give or take a few dozen faster ones.
Drive's humming along, last I checked. I listen to it like a safecracker listens to a lock.
Range is decent, {to}. More would be nice. More is always nice.
I've had drives quit on me mid getaway. This one hasn't, and I treat it like royalty for that.
The frame shift is fine. Every jump it makes, I'm a little bit prouder and a little bit surprised.
We can leave anywhere fast, {to}. That's the one feature I check twice.
Trust me, the drive's in good hands. Slightly sticky hands, but good ones.
Want more range? Find me an engineer who owes me a favour. There's a few out there.
Look, {to}, the drive and I have a deal. It keeps jumping, I keep my hands off its wiring.
I could squeeze another light year out of it. Wouldn't be legal, wouldn't be safe, but I could.
It's running cool and clean. Like a forged permit nobody's looked at twice.
scoundrel_profane: Drive's running like a dream, {to}. A weird, humming, damn expensive dream.
Range is fine. Could be better. Everything could be better, that's what credits are for.
Hell, the drive's in better shape than I am, and I'm gorgeous.
That hum? That's the sound of money well spent, {to}. Quit worrying.
I tuned this drive with a spanner and a lot of colourful language. Works like a charm.
If this drive ever quits, it quits when we're parked. We have a deal, and it knows I'm a vindictive bastard.
Frame shift's fine, {to}. If it weren't, you'd hear me screaming long before any alarm.
Want more speed? Get me to an engineer and a pile of credits, and I'll make this crate haul ass.
Drive's sweet. I check it every watch, because getting stranded out here would be a shit way to go.
{to}, relax. This drive's outrun customs, debt collectors and one very angry Hutton twin.
Jump range is what it is. If you want miracles, go to church. If you want a fast getaway, come to me.
Drive's sound, {to}. I'm not saying it's perfect, I'm saying I'd bet a damn good bottle on it.

scoundrel: {to}, how's the old girl holding together?
{to}, anything on this ship that needs fixing before it needs replacing?
{to}, what would you upgrade first if credits were no object?
{to}, honest opinion. Is {ship} worth what we paid for it?
{to}, how are the modules looking? Anything I should bribe someone to replace?
So {to}, is the hull as solid as it looks, or is that just good paint?
{to}, do you ever talk to the ship? Asking because I caught myself doing it.
{to}, if something broke right now, what's the first thing you'd grab?
What's the most expensive thing on this ship, and how fast could we sell it?
{to}, any repairs you've been putting off? I won't tell the boss. Much.
Is the ship in good shape, or is everyone just being polite?
{to}, give me the short version. Ship good, ship bad, or ship weird?
scoundrel_profane: {to}, is this tub holding together, or are we flying a damn miracle?
{to}, what's the worst thing wrong with the ship? Don't sugarcoat that crap.
{to}, how much would it cost to make this ship less of a heap? Ballpark.
{to}, the modules all behaving? Or are some of them being little bastards?
{to}, ever think {ship} has a personality? Because I swear it hates me.
{to}, any repairs we're dodging? You can tell me. I'm great at dodging things.
Who signed off on this paint job, and can we get our money back?
{to}, how's the hull? I keep hearing creaks and it's freaking the hell out of me.
{to}, what's the one module you'd steal for this ship if nobody was watching?
Is anything on this boat actually brand new, or is it all secondhand junk?
{to}, straight answer. Would this ship survive one of the boss's landings? Asking for all of us.
{to}, if the ship was a horse, would we have shot it by now? Damn, that came out wrong.

scoundrel: Ship's solid, {to}. A few scuffs, a few rattles. Character, I call it.
Everything's working that should be working. The rest I don't talk about.
I've kept worse wrecks flying on tape and charm. This one's practically new.
Modules are fine, near as I can tell. I check them like I check my winnings.
{to}, the ship's in better shape than any ship I ever borrowed. And I returned most of those.
Hull's holding. I patched it, polished it and told it it's pretty. Works every time.
If something needs fixing, I'll fix it. If it needs replacing, I know a guy with no paperwork.
Trust me, {to}. This ship's tougher than it looks, and it looks pretty tough.
Upgrades? Get me near an outfitting desk with a fat wallet and watch me go.
She's fine. Purring, mostly. Every so often she grumbles, but who doesn't?
Relax, {to}. If anything were actually wrong, I'd be the first one heading for the escape pod.
Ship's good. I sleep fine at night, and I've slept aboard some very dodgy ships.
scoundrel_profane: Ship's fine, {to}. Ugly as hell in places, but fine.
Everything works. The bits that don't work I've hidden behind panels so the boss doesn't see.
Hull's solid. I've patched worse with gum and a damn good lie to the inspector.
{to}, this ship's held together better than my last three schemes put together.
Modules are behaving, last I checked. If one starts acting up, I'll kick its ass back into line.
Honestly? I've stolen ships in worse shape. And sold them for a profit. Don't ask.
Repairs? Done. Mostly. The rest is cosmetic crap nobody looks at.
Trust me, {to}. If the ship were in trouble, I'd be a lot louder than this.
She creaks, she groans, she complains. Just like me, and I'm damn reliable.
Upgrades would be nice, {to}. Get me some credits and a shady outfitter and I'll work magic.
Ship's good. Not pretty, not new, but good. Like most of my friends.
Look, I'm not saying the ship's perfect. I'm saying I'd fly the shit out of it any day.

scoundrel: {to}, what's the going rate for space moss these days?
{to}, how do you tell a valuable plant from a worthless one? Besides the price tag.
{to}, what's the weirdest thing you've ever sampled out there?
{to}, is exobiology actually hard, or do you just make it look hard so we tip you?
{to}, which of these alien critters pays the best? Give me names.
So {to}, do the plants out here mind being sampled, or is that a silly question?
{to}, any life on the planets ahead worth a stop? I like easy money.
Who decided we should get paid for picking weeds on other planets, and can I thank them?
{to}, how far apart do the samples have to be, and why does it feel like a scam?
{to}, ever found something nobody's ever found before? What's that pay?
{to}, tell me straight. Is any of this stuff edible?
Anyone know what the most expensive bug in the galaxy is? Because I want one.
scoundrel_profane: {to}, what's the deal with this alien moss? Is it worth a damn?
{to}, which plants pay? Skip the boring crap, just give me the money ones.
{to}, how hard is it to sample a weird rock plant without getting your ass eaten?
{to}, ever sample something that tried to fight back?
{to}, how much do the big ticket critters go for? Roughly. I'm daydreaming.
{to}, be honest. Do you actually know what half these things are, or do you just scan and pray?
Why the hell does a bacterium pay better than an honest day's work?
{to}, what's the most valuable thing growing out here that nobody's grabbed yet?
{to}, any life down there worth the hike, or is it all the cheap shit?
{to}, do you name the samples? I'd name them after people who owe me money.
Who's in charge of the bug collecting today? Because I'm not getting out of my damn chair.
{to}, is exobiology the easiest money in the galaxy, or am I missing a catch?

scoundrel: Easy money, {to}. Find it, scan it, three samples, cash out. Like lifting snacks from a settlement.
The rare ones pay like a jewellery heist, and they don't have alarms. Mostly.
Just pick it up. That's the whole secret. The universe is leaving money on the ground.
First footfall plus a first sample? They pay extra for that. Now we're talking.
Honestly, {to}, I don't care what it's called. I care what it's worth.
Some of these things are pretty, I'll grant you. Pretty and profitable. My favourite combination.
I've sampled things that looked like rocks, rocks that looked like things, and one thing I'm still not sure about.
The trick is the distance between samples. Like fencing goods, you don't sell it all in one spot.
{to}, every sample's a little parcel of credits waiting for a buyer. I'm just the courier.
The good stuff likes certain planets. I've got a nose for it, same as I've got a nose for a soft mark.
Easiest customers I've ever had, {to}. They don't haggle, they don't complain, and they never call the cops.
{to}, if Vista Genomics ever stops paying, I'm going back to smuggling, and I'm taking the scanner.
scoundrel_profane: {to}, it's the easiest damn money in the galaxy. Walk up, scan, walk away rich.
Bacteria pay peanuts. The fancy stuff, though? That's a sweet little score.
Hell, I've lifted data off settlement desks that paid worse than one decent plant.
Three samples, spaced out, then go get paid. It's not rocket science, it's weed science.
{to}, I don't know what half of it is. I know what it sells for, and that's what counts.
First to sample something? Bonus. Bonus means I get the good bottle. Damn right it does.
Some of these critters are ugly as sin, but money doesn't care about looks.
A spiky thing nearly took my suit apart once. Took the sample anyway. Greedy, not stupid.
The rule is distance, {to}. Wander far enough between samples or the scanner gets all pissy.
Exobiology's a grift where the mark's a plant. Can't call the cops, can't run away. Beautiful.
Worth it? {to}, I've crawled through worse shit for half the pay.
Keep me pointed at planets with life and I'll keep the credits coming. That's the deal.

scoundrel: {to}, what's the strangest thing you've seen out here? And does it pay?
{to}, why do some stars look like they're about to explode? Should I be worried?
{to}, any planets coming up worth a closer look? A pretty one, a rich one, either works.
{to}, what makes a planet worth more on the market? Rings? Water? Good looks?
{to}, you ever look at a neutron star and think, that's a lot of free energy just sitting there?
So {to}, is space actually beautiful, or do I just need a drink?
{to}, which kind of star pays the best when we sell the data?
Anyone ever figure out why the black out here is so black?
{to}, what's a black hole look like up close, and how close is too close?
{to}, got any space trivia? Something I can use to impress people at a bar.
Ever wonder who'd buy a planet, if planets were for sale?
{to}, what's the rarest thing in the sky out here? Something I could brag about.
scoundrel_profane: {to}, what's the weirdest damn thing you've spotted out here?
{to}, is that star supposed to look like that, or should we be running like hell?
{to}, which planets are worth the scan? I'm not wasting time on cheap rocks.
{to}, tell me something about stars that isn't boring as crap.
{to}, how close could we get to a black hole before our asses got stretched?
{to}, does anything out here actually pay, or is it all just pretty?
Why the hell are there so many stars and so few bars?
{to}, what's the big deal with terraformable worlds? Why do they pay so well?
{to}, honestly, do you get tired of looking at the same damn sky?
{to}, any strange signals or weird stuff out here I should know about before I sleep?
Who names these stars? Because whoever it is needs a better imagination.
{to}, give me your favourite planet type. Mine's the one with a bar.

scoundrel: Out here, {to}, every star's a lottery ticket. Most lose. Some pay out big.
Earth-likes are the jackpot. Water worlds are close. Ammonia worlds, a nice little bonus.
Stars are pretty, sure. But you know what's prettier? A first discovery tag with my name on it.
I've seen gas giants that'd make a Hutton showgirl blush. Big, bright and very well rounded.
Neutron stars are like loan sharks, {to}. They'll speed you up, but they take a cut if you're careless.
Black holes? Lovely to look at, terrible to visit. Like a casino at Jameson.
The strange stuff is out there, {to}. Most of it doesn't pay, but it makes a good story at the bar.
Funny thing. I never cared about stars until I learned they pay extra for being first.
Ringed planets photograph well and sell well. I approve of anything that does both.
{to}, the universe is mostly empty and mostly rocks. The trick is finding the rocks worth money.
Every star I map, someone back home pays me for it. Feels like stealing, and I'd know.
Honestly, {to}? I only look up when the scanner pings. Then I look up a lot.
scoundrel_profane: Most of these stars are worth squat, {to}. But the good ones? Damn, they pay.
Earth-likes are the big score. Everything else is pocket change and pretty colours.
Strange stuff out here? Hell yes. Pays? Usually not. Story at the bar? Always.
Black holes are gorgeous and they'd eat us alive. Kind of like the Hutton twins.
{to}, I've seen nebulae that look like a spilled drink at a dive bar. Prettier, though.
Gas giants are big and mostly worthless. Like my uncle, but with better weather.
A neutron star is a damn slingshot, {to}. Treat it with respect or it'll fling you into next week.
The sky's beautiful, sure. Can't spend beautiful. Can spend a first discovery, though.
Water worlds are a nice payday. I'd marry one if the paperwork weren't such a pain in the ass.
{to}, I look at stars the way a pickpocket looks at a crowd. Who's carrying?
Space is mostly nothing with a few rocks in it, and every so often a rock that pays like crazy.
Honestly, the strangest thing out here is how much crap people will pay to know about a planet.

scoundrel: {to}, what's the data in the hold worth? Roughly. I'm planning a party.
{to}, how much is all this exploration going to pay us when we cash in?
{to}, what's my cut looking like? Not that I'm counting. I'm counting.
{to}, where do we get the best price for the data? I don't want to be fleeced.
{to}, if we sold everything we've got right now, could we afford something shiny?
So {to}, are we rich yet? Ballpark. Round up.
{to}, how do you keep track of who gets what? I'm told I need supervision.
Is anyone actually writing down what we're owed, or are we trusting the boss?
{to}, what's the smartest thing to do with a pile of credits? Besides give them to me.
{to}, ever think about how much we'd lose if we got blown up with all this data aboard?
Anybody know if Universal Cartographics takes tips? I'd like to grease that wheel.
{to}, how much is one first discovery worth these days?
scoundrel_profane: {to}, how much is this damn data worth, and when do I get my cut?
{to}, are we rich yet, or still just broke with a nice view?
{to}, what's the take looking like? And don't give me that hard to say crap.
{to}, how much would we lose if some bastard blew us up right now?
{to}, who's buying the first round when we cash in? Because it sure as hell isn't me.
{to}, does the data sell better if we hold onto it, or is that just a story?
Who the hell decided explorers only get paid when they get home?
{to}, how are the books? Anyone skimming? Besides me, I mean.
{to}, honest guess. What's the payday when we hit a station?
{to}, if I stole a little off the top, would you even notice?
When do we get paid? I've got debts and a reputation to keep up, damn it.
{to}, what's the deal with the bonus for being first? Is it worth the extra jumps?

scoundrel: Data's worth plenty, {to}. Not retire on a beach plenty, but buy a nice dinner plenty.
Your cut's safe with me. Well, safe-ish. I keep very creative books.
Everything we scan is money in the hold. Invisible money. The best kind, nobody can lift it but us.
First discoveries pay a bonus. I love a bonus. A bonus is a tip from the universe.
{to}, I keep the numbers in my head. That way nobody can audit them.
Sell it all at once, I say. Spread it out and somebody always asks questions.
Honestly, {to}? We're doing fine. Not Robigo fine, but fine.
Credits are like friends. Never enough, and they disappear when you need them.
The best price? Any station with a cartographics desk and a short memory.
I'm counting every credit, {to}. Twice. Once for the books and once for me.
If we got blown up now, we'd lose the lot. So let's not. That's my whole financial plan.
Trust me, {to}. When we cash in, the bar's going to love us.
scoundrel_profane: We're sitting on a decent pile, {to}. Not a fortune, but a damn good start.
Your cut's coming. Minus expenses. Minus fees. Minus my tip. You'll get something, I swear.
The data's worth more the further we go. Hell, out here, every rock's a little paycheque.
{to}, I've cooked better books than these, and nobody caught me. Well, almost nobody.
Sell it all in one go. Spread it out and some nosy bastard at the desk starts asking questions.
First discovery bonus? Free money for being somewhere first. Best racket going.
Honestly? We're doing fine. Not a Hutton twin on each arm fine, but fine.
{to}, if we die out here, all that data goes with us. So please don't let the boss do anything stupid as shit.
Credits are just points in a game, and I intend to win the damn game.
I count every credit, {to}. You'd think I was a banker. A crooked one, sure, but a banker.
We'll cash in eventually. And when we do, the drinks are on the boss.
Worth? Enough to make it worth it. More if the boss quits dragging us past the crappy systems.

scoundrel: {to}, what's the best ore to dig if you want to get rich quick?
{to}, ever pulled a motherlode out of a rock? What's it feel like?
{to}, how do you tell a good rock from a boring rock? They all look the same to me.
{to}, are we doing any mining this trip, or are the rigs just decoration?
{to}, what's the most valuable thing you've ever cracked open?
So {to}, is mining honest work? Because I'm told I should try some.
{to}, how much would a hold full of painite fetch these days?
Who decided rocks in space should be worth money? Genius, whoever it was.
{to}, does mining ever get boring, or is every rock a little gamble?
{to}, what's your favourite way to crack a rock? Lasers, charges, or harsh language?
Anyone know where the good rings are around here? Asking for profit.
{to}, if you found a fortune in an asteroid, would you tell the rest of us?
scoundrel_profane: {to}, what's the damn ore that pays the most? I want names.
{to}, how do you stand chipping at rocks all day without losing your mind?
{to}, ever blow up a rock and get nothing but crap?
{to}, how much painite would it take to retire? Asking for my future self.
{to}, are we ever going to mine this trip, or is that kit just dead weight?
{to}, is it true a good core can pay like hell? Or is that miner bullshit?
Why the hell do I find rocks fascinating now? This trip's broken me.
{to}, what's the trick to cracking a core without blowing your own ass off?
{to}, if I helped mine, would I get a cut, or just sore arms?
{to}, honest answer. Is mining the most boring way to get rich?
Anyone else think asteroids look like big lumpy credits? No? Just me?
{to}, which ring's worth the trip, and which ones are a waste of damn time?

scoundrel: Painite, {to}. Painite, low temperature diamonds, void opals. Dig those and buy a moon.
Every rock is a little safe. You just need the right tools and a bit of patience. I know safes.
Mining's honest work. I hate that about it. But the pay's nice.
I cracked a core once and it paid more than three Robigo runs. Nearly made me go straight.
{to}, the rigs are ready whenever the boss finds a ring worth the bother.
Good rocks light up on the scanner. Boring rocks just sit there, like guards on a night shift.
Truth is, mining's like fencing goods. Find the stuff, haul it, sell it before anyone asks.
{to}, I tell everyone about the good rocks. Eventually. After I've had a look.
Lasers for the easy stuff, charges for the cores. Harsh language for everything else.
The trick is knowing where to dig. I've got a nose for buried treasure. Always have.
Out here, mining's a hobby. Back near a market, it's a business. I prefer business.
{to}, the biggest score I ever pulled out of a rock paid for a very long weekend at Hutton.
scoundrel_profane: Painite, {to}. Damn near pure profit if you find a good hotspot.
Every rock's a gamble. Most are crap. One in a hundred makes you a king.
I once blew a core so clean the whole crew cheered. Then we sold it and cheered louder.
Mining's honest work, {to}, and I hate honest work. But hell, the money's honest too.
The rigs are ready. Point me at a ring and get out of my way.
Is it boring? Sure. Boring as shit. But boring and rich beats exciting and broke.
Cracking cores is like cracking safes. Find the weak spot, set the charge, keep your fingers.
{to}, I'd tell you where the good rings are, but then I'd have to charge you.
Void opals, {to}. Pretty, rare and worth a damn fortune. My kind of rock.
Lasers, limpets, a lot of cursing. That's mining. Anyone who says otherwise is selling something.
I've mined rocks that paid more than my first three ships combined. Granted, those ships were crap.
Mining's just stealing from asteroids, and they never press charges.

scoundrel: {to}, if pirates showed up, what's the plan? Please say running.
{to}, how often do you check our six out here? Ballpark.
{to}, what's the best way to slip an interdiction? I've got my own ideas.
{to}, is anybody out here dangerous, or are we safe as houses?
{to}, ever been interdicted by someone you owed money? Asking for me.
So {to}, do we fight or do we fly, if it ever comes to it?
{to}, what scares you most out here? Thargoids, pirates, or the boss's driving?
Anyone know if the fuzz patrols this far out? Not that I've got anything to hide.
{to}, how are the shields holding up, just in case?
{to}, tell me silent running works. I need to hear it.
Who's watching for trouble while I'm napping?
{to}, what's the safest thing we can do if someone comes knocking?
scoundrel_profane: {to}, if some bastard interdicts us, we're running, right? Tell me we're running.
{to}, how dangerous is it out here, really? Spare me the tactical crap.
{to}, what's your move when a pirate gets cocky? Mine's boost and swear.
{to}, anybody tailing us? I've got a feeling, and my feelings are usually right as hell.
{to}, how good are our odds against a real fighter? Be honest. Actually, don't.
{to}, do Thargoids come out this far, or is that just scary bar talk?
Who the hell would bother pirating explorers? We carry data and bad coffee.
{to}, what's the trick to dodging scans? I want to compare notes.
{to}, shields up to snuff? I'd hate to get my ass handed to me by some punk.
{to}, if we got jumped, how long would we last? Rough number.
Is anybody watching the scanner, or are we all just admiring the damn view?
{to}, what's the meanest thing you've ever done to a pirate?

scoundrel: The plan, {to}, is the same as always. Boost, dodge, jump. Heroics are for people who don't value their skin.
Out here, the worst threat is usually us. Bad landings, hot stars, the boss's ideas.
Silent running, a cold ship and a fast jump. I've slipped past customs with less.
I watch the scanner like a fence watches the door. Nothing's getting close without me knowing.
Interdiction? Submit, boost, jump. Fighting's for people with insurance and something to prove.
{to}, I don't fight fair, I don't fight long, and I don't fight at all if I can run.
Pirates this far out would be rare, I reckon. Not much here worth stealing but our good looks.
Trust me, {to}. I've outrun the fuzz at Lave twice. A pirate out here doesn't scare me.
Safest thing we can do? Stay boring. Nobody robs a boring ship.
{to}, the shields are fine and my escape plan is better. Sleep easy.
I keep an eye out. Not because I'm brave. Because I'm very, very attached to me.
If something nasty shows up, {to}, the first words you'll hear from me are punch it.
scoundrel_profane: If anyone jumps us, {to}, we run like hell. That's not cowardice, that's a business plan.
Pirates out here? Not likely. There's nothing to steal but data and the boss's dignity.
Interdiction's simple. Submit, boost, jump, swear loudly. In that order. Damn effective.
I don't do fair fights, {to}. Fair fights are for idiots and dead people.
Silent running's my specialty. I've hidden from better scanners than any pirate's got, trust me.
Thargoids? If I see one, I'm out of here so fast my shadow gets left holding the damn bag.
Shields are fine, {to}. And if they're not, the drive is, and the drive is what counts.
Trust me, I've been chased by meaner bastards than anything out here.
Safest move? Stay quiet, stay cold, stay dull. Hell, nobody even looks twice at a dull ship.
{to}, I watch that scanner like it owes me money. Nothing sneaks up on us.
Fighting is how you lose the cargo, the ship and the bar tab. Running is how you keep all three.
{to}, if it ever comes to it, I'll handle the dodging. You handle holding on and not puking on my shit.

scoundrel: {to}, heard anything interesting on the comms lately? Gossip counts.
{to}, do other commanders ever chat out here, or is it just us and the static?
{to}, what's the funniest thing you've ever overheard on station traffic?
{to}, ever pick up a distress call that turned out to be a scam? Asking professionally.
{to}, how do you stand listening to station control all day? Same lines, every time.
So {to}, anyone out here we should be saying hello to? Or avoiding?
{to}, is it true traffic control can hear us complaining about them?
Anybody ever get a message from someone who owes them money? No? Just me, then.
{to}, what's the quickest way to sweet talk a docking controller?
{to}, picked up any signals worth chasing? Money signals, ideally.
Is it quiet out here, or is the radio just broken?
{to}, if I wanted to send a message to a certain pair of twins at Hutton, how would I do it?
scoundrel_profane: {to}, anything on the comms? Or is it the same dead static as always, damn it?
{to}, any other pilots out here chattering, or are we alone as hell?
{to}, what's the dumbest crap you've heard on an open channel?
{to}, can you fake a docking request? Hypothetically. For science.
{to}, do station controllers ever crack a joke, or are they all dead inside?
{to}, who'd you most like to block on the comms? I've got a list.
Why the hell does station traffic always sound bored to tears?
{to}, anybody broadcasting out here worth listening to?
{to}, ever heard a distress call that was a total con? I ran one once. It was a beauty.
{to}, picked up anything from those twins at Hutton? They said they'd write. Damn liars.
Is anyone actually listening to the radio, or is it just me and the noise?
{to}, how do you talk to pirates on comms without pissing them off?

scoundrel: Quiet out here, {to}. Just static, the odd beacon and my own lovely voice.
Station traffic is the same five sentences, forever. I could do the controller's job asleep.
Other pilots out here? Rare as an honest fence. Now and then, a hello.
I've heard distress calls that were real, and distress calls that were mine. Long story.
{to}, the trick with docking control is to sound polite and slightly confused. Works every time.
Gossip? The bubble's always buzzing. Out here it's just me listening to the stars hiss.
The best thing I ever heard on open comms was a smuggler explaining his cargo was decorative.
{to}, I can sweet talk any controller in the bubble. It's a gift, and they never see it coming.
If anyone's out here, they're keeping quiet. Smart. I'd do the same.
I used to run a little racket faking permits over comms. Strictly small time. Strictly in the past.
{to}, the channels are clean, last I looked. Nobody hailing, nobody hunting.
I keep a channel open for the Hutton twins, {to}. Years now. Nothing. The rest of the comms out here are about as chatty.
scoundrel_profane: Nothing on the comms, {to}. Just static and the occasional damn beacon.
Station control's the most boring job in the galaxy. Same crap, every docking, forever.
Pilots out here? Hardly any. And the ones I hear are either lost or full of shit.
{to}, I once talked my way past a customs cutter with a fake accent and a lot of nerve.
Docking control is easy. Be polite, sound harmless and never, ever argue with the bastards.
If anyone's listening, they're doing it quietly. Smart people. Hell, I'd do the same.
{to}, the open channel's like a dive bar. Mostly noise, and the occasional idiot starting trouble.
Distress calls out here are rare. Real ones, anyway. The fake ones I used to send were gorgeous.
{to}, I'll let you know if anyone worth a damn says hello. Don't hold your breath.
Channels are clear, last I checked. Peaceful. Suspiciously peaceful, if you ask me.
The best thing I ever heard on comms? A pirate trying to sound scary while his voice cracked. Poor bastard. Good times.
I can sweet talk any controller, {to}. Except at Lave. Lave hates my guts, and fair enough.

scoundrel: {to}, what do you make of the boss's flying lately? Honest answer.
{to}, does our fearless leader actually have a plan, or is it all instinct?
{to}, what's the boss's worst habit? I've got a guess.
{to}, ever disagree with the boss and win?
{to}, how do you keep our fearless leader out of trouble? Asking so I can do the opposite.
So {to}, would you follow the boss into a black hole? Hypothetically.
{to}, what's the best call the boss ever made? Besides hiring me.
Does the boss ever sleep, or is that just a rumour?
{to}, is it me, or does our fearless leader land like they're angry at the planet?

Out of ten? Seven, on a good day. On a bad day the boss scares the shit out of me.

I've been thinking about those twins at Hutton. Don't ask. Seriously, don't.
{to}, I once spent a whole watch counting the bolts on this deck. Two hundred and twelve. Damn tedious.
Quiet watches are for napping with one eye open. Old smuggler's trick.
Time drags like a drunk at closing. You just ride it out and hope nobody throws up.
{to}, sit tight. The universe owes us a little excitement, and it always pays up eventually.
Cards? Sure. Deal me in. I'll take your cut and your dignity, nothing personal.

{to}, who in your family would you call if you needed bail? Hypothetically.

Got family waiting for you somewhere, {to}?
So who raised you? Somebody must take the blame.

{to}, family. Good memories or the other kind?

{to}, your folks. Straight arrows, or crooked as hell like mine?

scoundrel: My ma ran a bar on the lower ring of an old station in Diso. I grew up under the counter, learning to spot a mark.
Pa was in the import business, {to}. Mostly the part where things got imported without the paperwork.
My uncle Vic ran the card game in Ma's back room. Taught me to shuffle at six, deal from the bottom at seven.
Big sister Dee is a customs officer now. Can you believe that? Family dinners are very tense.
Nana Rosa was the best card cheat on the station. Took me years to figure out how she did it. Still not sure.
Loud, {to}. Loud, crooked, and loving. In that order, mostly.
Cousins everywhere. You couldn't throw a stolen wrench on that ring without hitting one of us.
Ma always said: I don't care what you do, just don't get caught, and call on holidays. I manage about half of that.
Honestly, {to}? Good people. Bad habits, but good people.
Pa disappeared for a year when I was nine. Came back with a tan and a new ship. Nobody asked.
We weren't rich, but we always ate. Funny how much fell off the backs of freighters on our ring.
Dee still sends me a message every birthday, {to}. It's always the same: I know what you did. Sweet, really.
scoundrel_profane: Ma could break up a bar fight with one look and a frying pan. Toughest damn woman on the ring.
Pa? Import business, {to}. The kind where the paperwork goes missing, and so does Pa, for months at a time.
Uncle Vic ran the card game in Ma's back room. Cheated like a bastard. Taught me everything.
My big sister Dee is a customs officer now. A damn customs officer. Holidays are a hostage situation.
Nana Rosa cheated at cards till the day she died. Best of us. Hell, she probably cheated at that too.
Loud, {to}. Loud as hell, crooked and loving. Mostly in that order.
Cousins everywhere. Throw a hot wrench on that ring and you'd hit three of us.
Ma had one rule: don't get caught, and call on holidays. I'm about fifty fifty on that.
Every one of them could pick a lock, {to}. Presents were never wrapped, just liberated. Hell of a family.
Pa vanished for a year when I was nine. Came back with a tan and a ship nobody had the guts to ask about.
We were broke, but we ate. Amazing how much food fell off freighters on our ring. Pure damn luck, I'm sure.
Dee messages me every birthday, {to}: I know what you did. Doesn't say which thing. Smart cookie.

scoundrel: {to}, where'd you grow up? Somewhere nice, or somewhere interesting?

The lower ring, {to}. Where the rent was cheap and the questions were cheaper.
Diso. Close enough to Lave to see the money, far enough that none of it reached us.
Grew up in the corridors behind Ma's bar. Best education in the galaxy, if you want to learn to lie.
Home was a station where the air scrubbers coughed and so did everybody else. I loved it.
My ring had one rule, {to}: what happens on the lower ring stays on the lower ring. And it did. Mostly.
I used to sit at the big window on the observation deck and watch the traders come in. Picking out marks, mostly.
Diso. Never been back. Well, once. In disguise. Long story.

Diso, {to}. If you go, try the noodle stand on the lower ring. Tell them I sent you. Then run.

The lower ring, {to}. Cheap rent, cheaper questions, and nobody gave a damn who you were.
Diso. Close enough to Lave to smell the money, far enough that none of the bastards ever shared.

Diso. Been back once, in disguise. Don't ask. Seriously, don't.
Every shop on the lower ring sold something, {to}. Half of it pinched from the other half.
Home was a bunk over a bar and a lot of yelling. Now it's wherever we dock. Better plumbing, at least.
You either got out of that place or it ate you. I got out. Through a cargo hatch, at a dead run.
Diso, {to}. Try the noodle stand on the lower ring. Mention my name, then run like hell.

We dock tomorrow, what are you stuffing your face with first?

Worst, {to}? Three days hiding in a cargo hold on nothing but ration bars and fear. The fear tasted better.
Ma's noodle soup, from the bar. Nobody knew what was in it. Nobody asked. Best thing in the galaxy.
Detention block breakfast at Lave. Synthetic eggs. I only stayed one night, but the eggs stayed with me for a week.
I had dinner once with the Hutton twins, {to}. Can't remember the food. Can't forget the dessert. You know.
Lavian brandy, the real stuff, not the fake I used to sell. Turns out the fake was better. Who knew.
There's a noodle stand on the lower ring back home. Four credits a bowl. I'd fly a thousand light years for one right now.
Worst ever was a street pie at Sothis. I won't say what was in it, because the vendor never would either.
Best meal's always the free one, {to}. Second best is the one somebody else thinks they're paying for.
Uncle Vic made a stew every time a card game went well. We ate a lot of stew. He was very good at cards.
Lifted a crate of fancy chocolates off a settlement once. Ate the evidence. Best crime I ever committed.
Honestly, {to}? Anything hot. Spend enough nights eating cold out of a smuggler's hold, and hot is a luxury.
scoundrel_profane: Real steak in Lave, the night the Robigo payout cleared. Tipped like an idiot. Worth every damn credit.
Worst, {to}? Three days in a cargo hold on ration bars. Tasted like cardboard and bad decisions.
Ma's noodle soup. Nobody knew what the hell was in it. Nobody dared ask. Perfect.
Lave detention block, synthetic eggs. One night inside, and that crap haunted me for a week.
Dinner with the Hutton twins, {to}. Couldn't tell you what we ate. Could tell you about dessert, but you'd blush. Hell, I'd blush.
Real Lavian brandy, not the knock-off I used to sell. Turns out the knock-off was better. Ain't that some shit.
Noodle stand on the lower ring back home. Cheap as dirt, and I'd fly the whole bubble for one bowl right now.
Street pie at Sothis. Never found out what was in it. The bastard selling them wouldn't say either.
Best meal's the free one, {to}. Second best is the one some other sucker's paying for.
Uncle Vic made stew whenever a card game went his way. We ate a hell of a lot of stew.
Swiped a crate of fancy chocolates off a settlement once. Ate the evidence. Sick as a dog. Worth it.
Honestly, {to}? Anything hot. Eat cold out of a smuggler's hold for a month and a hot meal makes you cry like a baby.

{to}, if you could live one day over again, which one?

{to}, luckiest day you ever had? Spill.

scoundrel: The day the big Robigo payout cleared, {to}. I checked my balance forty times. It was still there every time.
That card game at Jameson. Walked in with forty credits, walked out with a Cobra. Didn't keep it long, but what a night.
Got scanned by the cops at Lave with a hold full of hot cargo. Walked away clean. Best day and worst day, same hour.
The Hutton twins. That's all I'm going to say. Okay, I'll say one more thing: wow.
First time Uncle Vic let me deal the back-room game, {to}. Took the whole table. He's never been prouder.
The day I got my first ship. Well. Got it. Borrowed it. Details.
Day I outran three police Vipers out of Sothis. Heat sinks popping, canopy cracking, me laughing like a maniac.
Honestly, {to}? Every payday. They're all my best day while they last.
Sold a forged permit to a guy who turned out to be a customs officer. Off duty. He loved it. Bought two more.
The day Dee made customs officer, {to}. I sent flowers. Borrowed flowers, but still, it's the thought.
The day a fence at Sothis paid me double for a crate of junk because I told him it was antique. It was old. Junk ages.
Ma's bar, my birthday, the whole lower ring came. Half of them were wanted. Best party ever.

Card game at Jameson. Forty credits in, a whole Cobra out. Lost the bastard by morning, but what a night.
Lave cops scanned me with a hold full of hot cargo and I walked. Nearly fainted, then bought drinks for the whole bar.
The Hutton twins. That's it. That's the story. Okay, one more word: damn.
First time Uncle Vic let me run the back-room game, {to}. Cleaned out the whole table. Cheated like hell. He cried.
Day I got my first ship. Got, borrowed, same shit.
The night I talked a station guard out of a full cargo scan with nothing but a smile and a bottle of brandy. Smooth as shit.
Honestly, {to}? Payday. Every single one. Best day of my life, over and over, till the money runs out.
Sold a forged permit to an off-duty customs officer. Bastard loved it. Came back for two more.
The day Dee made customs officer, {to}. Sent her flowers. Hot flowers, sure, but it's the damn thought.
Sold a fence at Sothis a crate of junk as antiques. Doubled my money. Hell, it was old junk. Technically antique.
My birthday at Ma's bar. Whole lower ring showed up, half of them wanted. Best party in the history of that dump.
